title: Pixel 11 Pro vs. Pixel 10 Pro
description: The new Pixel 11 series is now out so new and returning customers have started making their comparisons. And we are doing our best to help with a more detailed look at the most popular ones. Pixel 11 Pro or Pixel 10 Pro? Let’s find out! The 256GB base version of the Google Pixel 11 Pro is quite pricey at €1,100, while the 128GB base model of the Google Pixel 10 Pro now sits at a far more reasonable price of €770. Is it worth paying the premium for the Google Pixel 11 Pro then? Table of Contents: Design Display Battery Life Charging Speaker Test Performance ...

title: Samsung to outsource all of its DRAM manufacturing and focus on HBM production
description: The AI race is heating up, and so is the demand for hardware required to support it. That's why companies that produce HBM memory chips like Samsung have benefited immensely in the last few years. So it's only logical for Samsung to shift its focus to HBM memory production, as this is the company's best-performing business lately. According to inside sources, Samsung is already in talks with its partners, urging them to finish their DDR5 production lines ahead of schedule and is looking to invest in new outsourced production lines as well. This will free up in-house capacity, which can...

title: iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max pre-orders in China eclipse the 2025 Pros
description: Pre-orders in the US may have been less than stellar, but the new iPhone 18 Pro models are a huge hit in China. Local publications report that a total of over 7 million units have been pre-ordered across all channels. Pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max started late in the evening of September 12 (Saturday) at 8pm. Retailer JD ran out of available units in under a minute. We don’t know how many units JD had on hand, but there are similar stories from other retailers. Sales revenue from iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max pre-orders on Tmall was double what the iPhone 17 Pro and...

title: Snap's Specs AR glasses are now on pre-order, Verizon is offering data plans for them
description: Snap, formerly known as Snapchat, spun off Specs, the division responsible for its augmented reality (AR) glasses, early this year, and now it's ready to take pre-orders for the upcoming product, which is also called Specs, just to be confusing. These are $2,195 standalone AR glasses that don't require a phone or computer connection to work. They have a see-through transparent display with a 51-degree field of view which apparently looks as big as a 115" screen would when viewed from about 10 feet away, a camera indicator light, "dual Snapdragon processors", and a magnetic 5-pin charging...

title: Here is when the Galaxy S25 and Galaxy Z7 series will receive the One UI 9 update
description: Samsung started rolling out the One UI 9 update for the Galaxy S26, S26+ and S26 Ultra yesterday (the S26 FE came with One UI 9 out of the box). However, the global press release doesn’t really mention older devices – there is a note about which models will get the Privacy Alerts feature, but nothing on when the actual update might arrive. Luckily, Samsung Thailand was more forthcoming with details on the timeline – the Galaxy S25 series and the Galaxy Z7 foldables will get One UI 9 on September 28. Samsung Galaxy S25 • Samsung Galaxy S25+ • Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra • Samsung...

title: Bose unveils new Ultra Open Earbuds and Sport Open Earbuds
description: Today Bose has unveiled the new Sport Open Earbuds and the Ultra Open Earbuds. Both of these are "designed to create more listening moments across active pursuits and everyday life", the company says. These second-generation Ultra Open Earbuds represent Bose's new flagship open-ear experience, while the new Sport Open Earbuds are the more affordable (yet still not cheap) option. The Ultra Open Earbuds have a newly engineered driver that delivers deeper bass and a higher volume than the first-gen model. Snapdragon Sound support is also there, with aptX Adaptive for high-quality audio....

title: Apple may do another price hike as it reportedly accepts Samsung's higher memory prices for next year
description: The new iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max launch tomorrow with price tags $100 higher than what their 2025 predecessors cost. Even older models from the iPhone 17 and 16 series weren’t spared the $100 price hike. Unfortunately, this isn’t the end of it and new reports claim that Apple will raise prices again next year. A couple of days ago, Korean publications reported that Samsung is renegotiating DRAM and NAND prices with smartphone manufacturers, including Apple. It seems that Samsung and Apple have now reached an agreement on the new prices. Apple will reportedly pay close to...

title: vivo X500 runs Geekbench, reveals a chipset schism in the line
description: The upcoming vivo X500 has seemingly been spotted in the Geekbench online database with the model number V2609A. As you can see in the screenshot below, the device managed a single-core score of 2,694 and a multi-core score of 7,770 in Geekbench 6.7.1 for Android. It's powered by a MediaTek chipset that could very well be the newly announced Dimensity 9600M - or it's the Dimensity 9500 from last year, it's hard to tell since the differences between the two aren't very big. The prototype which ran the benchmark had 12GB of RAM, but as always vivo may offer more options when the phone...

title: Huawei Mate 90 Pro Max key specifications surface
description: The Huawei Mate 90 series is expected to launch in October, and a new rumor has now surfaced, revealing the key specifications of the Mate 90 Pro Max. According to tipster Smart Pikachu on Weibo, the Huawei Mate 90 Pro Max will be powered by the Kirin 9050 Pro chipset, which also powers the company’s recently launched Mate XT 2 Ultimate Design tri-folding phone. Huawei Mate 80 Pro Max The tipster also claims that the phone will feature a next generation dual-layer OLED display and will be available with an optional privacy screen. For photography, the Mate 90 Pro Max is said to...

title: MediaTek Dimensity 9600M is also official
description: Earlier this week, MediaTek announced its latest flagship chipset – the Dimensity 9600 Pro and it turns out that’s not the only new SoC from the maker. The Dimensity 9600M is an upcoming chip that’s bringing some software and AI features from the 9600 Pro to a broader segment of flagship phones. From a hardware perspective, the 9600M is essentially a repackaged Dimensity 9500, fabbed on TSMC’s 3nm N3P process with identical components. It gets the same all-large-core CPU with a max frequency of 4.21GHz on the C1-Ultra core. The same applies to the Arm Mali-G1 Ultra MC12 GPU and the APU...

title: Galaxy Z Fold8 sales in Korea pick up after the announcement of the iPhone Duo
description: Korean publication The Chosun is reporting that sales of the Galaxy Z Fold8 increased by around 10% on a week-to-week basis just after Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo. Some people were holding off to see what Apple had cooked up before committing to a Z Fold8 or waiting for a Duo. Indeed, the Duo won’t come out until late October, while the wide Galaxy foldable is available now – this is quoted as one of the reasons for people picking the Samsung phone. However, this isn’t nearly the whole story. Samsung Galaxy Z Fold8 In Korea, Samsung is selling its phones more cheaply than...

title: Honor Win tablet is coming soon with an OLED display and built-in fan
description: The Honor Win lineup, which currently includes the Win, Win RT and Win Turbo smartphones, is set to expand with a new tablet. The company has revealed several details about the upcoming Honor Win tablet and offered a first look at its design. Honor China Smart Life business head Lin Lin shared a teaser of the Win tablet on Weibo, offering a first look at its rear design. The image shows a square-shaped camera module with Win branding on the back panel. The executive also confirmed that the tablet will feature a built-in cooling fan. In the comments section of the post, Lin Lin...

title: OnePlus 16 launch teased, 165Hz system-wide refresh rate confirmed
description: We’ve heard plenty about the OnePlus 16 through leaks and rumors, but the company has remained quiet about the upcoming flagship until now. OnePlus has officially teased the phone’s launch in China and confirmed some of its key specifications. In a post on Weibo, the company teased the launch of the OnePlus 16, saying that the phone is coming soon. A recent leak suggested that the flagship could be unveiled in October. OnePlus has confirmed that the phone will run Android 17 based ColorOS 17. The company also revealed that the OnePlus 16 will support a system-wide 165Hz refresh...

title: Google Pixel 11 review
Honor Win 2 and Win 2 RT get certified
description: According to the prolific leaker who goes by Digital Chat Station on Weibo, Honor's upcoming Win 2 and Win 2 RT smartphones may have just been certified for sale in China. The Win 2 supports 100W wired charging and the Win 2 RT goes up to 90W. That would be an interesting downgrade for the more affordable model, as the original Win RT supported 100W wired charging too. Anyway, DCS says the Win 2 will be the only phone released this year to pair Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 chipset with a battery over 10,000 mAh, a powerful built-in cooling fan, and an ultra-high refresh rate display...

title: iQOO shows the Pad Ultra and its dedicated gaming accessories
description: iQOO is launching the Pad Ultra in China on September 29 alongside the iQOO 16 smartphone. The company has, in the past few days, shown us the phone, and today it has decided to also present the tablet. So here it is in all its glory, the iQOO Pad Ultra. iQOO will offer a dual-sided gamepad for the device as well as a case with clip-on handles. Both of these are advertised as e-sports oriented, so clearly the tablet will be all about gaming. iQOO Pad Ultra official images The iQOO Pad Ultra will be available in silver and black. It has an 8.8-inch screen and weighs just...

title: Xiaomi 18 Pro runs Geekbench confirming its chipset
description: Yesterday Xiaomi finally started to officially tease the upcoming 18 Pro series, revealing that the Xiaomi 18 Pro and Xiaomi 18 Pro Max will be unveiled later this month (an exact date is yet to be announced). Today a Xiaomi device powered by the upcoming Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 Pro SoC was spotted in the Geekbench online database with the model number M154FF. That is a very new way for Xiaomi to do model numbers, by the way, as the company has so far been using a system that starts with the year and month. We're not saying the listing is fake, just that it's got a surprising model...

title: Honor MagicOS 11 debuts with liquid glass design and more capable AI
description: Honor announced its take on Android 17 with MagicOS 11 today at its Global Developer Conference. It brings an iOS-inspired liquid glass design, which Honor developed using its custom Luminous and Hummingbird base architectures. They optimize the user interface dynamics, AI processing, and hardware performance. Honor claims that despite the fancy new look, MagicOS 11 brings up to 20% faster system animations compared to MagicOS 10. The new system also features updated icons, menu items, widgets and customizable tinting for the home screen icons and dock. The other key addition...

title: The iPhone 18 Pro Max is the fastest-charging iPhone ever
description: Apple's iPhone 18 Pro Max will charge faster than any other iPhone ever. According to a new post by Ice Universe on X, the device goes from 0 to 50% charge in just 15 minutes. That is in fact what Apple claimed during the announcement. [#InlinePriceWidget,14716,1#] The iPhone 18 Pro Max takes just 10 minutes to reach 34%, and reports 100% charge after 55 minutes. However, it only stops charging after 76 minutes. In our review of its predecessor, we noted that it reached 38% after 15 minutes, and displayed 100% after 72 minutes. title: SK Hynix reportedly wants Intel to make its memory chips in the US
description: According to a new report from Reuters, SK Hynix is now in talks with Intel about a potential deal that would see the Korean company manufacture memory chips in the US for the first time. There are apparently two ways this can go: either SK Hynix will lease part of Intel's chip factory in Ohio, or it could form a joint venture with Intel as well as some unnamed "major cloud firms that are keen to lock in memory chip supplies". This all comes from "people familiar with the matter", so nothing is confirmed or official yet. A deal with SK Hynix would help Intel get out of its current not...
